title: Every Electron's Address Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A cinema seat, a train berth and a letter all need an address: a few numbers that point to exactly one spot. An atom can hold dozens of electrons, so how do chemists point to just one? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 2, Structure of Atom) we build the address of an electron with four quantum numbers.

You will see what an orbital is (the region where an electron is most likely to be found), then build every part of the address on the molecule bench: the principal quantum number n picks the shell (K, L, M, N), the azimuthal quantum number l picks the subshell and shape (s, p, d, f, with l from 0 to n - 1), the magnetic quantum number ml picks the orbital (from -l to +l, so 2l + 1 orbitals), and the spin quantum number ms is +1/2 or -1/2. A live counter shows the address of one electron in a 3p orbital. We then prove that a shell has n squared orbitals and holds at most 2n squared electrons, work out the M shell (9 orbitals, 18 electrons), and finish with the exam trap (there is no 1p or 2d), an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 22 of our PUC Chemistry series. Episode 21 covers the quantum mechanical model of the atom.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 Every electron needs an address
0:33 What is an orbital?
0:59 The four quantum numbers on the bench
2:13 Pause and think: which address can exist?
2:34 Orbitals in a shell: n squared
3:12 Worked example: the M shell
3:44 Exam trap: no 1p, no 2d
4:10 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
4:47 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Shapes of s, p and d Orbitals. Why is a p orbital shaped like a dumbbell, with nothing at its centre?
